function: CNN predicts the BS linear precoder, energy beamformer, STAR-RIS reflection and transmission phase shifts and user grouping that maximise short-packet spectral efficiency (p. 12).
system: Downlink MIMO-NOMA with SWIPT: BS 10 antennas, information users 2, energy users 1; four STAR-RISs (simultaneously transmitting and reflecting), 20+20 elements; band not stated (pp. 4, 13).
method: Supervised CNN (3 convolution blocks with batch normalisation and ReLU, then fully connected layer) trained offline to imitate the solutions of the inner-approximation algorithm (p. 12).
data_channel: Custom simulator: i.i.d. Rayleigh fading, Rician (K = 3 dB) for BS to STAR-RIS, path-loss exponent 2.7; 10K samples labelled by Algorithm 2 (pp. 4, 12, 13).
test_conditions: Training and testing on a random 80/10/10 split of one simulated dataset; no unseen scenario reported, though results sweep power, users, antennas, elements (pp. 12-16).
baselines: Non-learned: iterative AUG algorithm, random grouping, no grouping, brute-force search, no energy beamforming; learned: DNN of [7], CNN without scaling (pp. 13-16).
metrics: Average spectral efficiency, test-set RMSE of the predicted solution, iterations to converge, execution time (pp. 13-16).
complexity: Table II (p. 13): worst-case complexity of Algorithm 2 and brute force; Table V (p. 16): runtime 0.34-0.89 s CNN versus 74-1,150 s iterative.
q1_support: p. 4: "(i.i.d.) Rayleigh fading" and "Rician fading is utilized to model this transmission channel [27]"; own simulator with path-loss exponent 2.7 (p. 13). No 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 12: "the training, validations, and test sets with a ratio of 80-10-10" is a held-out part of the same data. Figs. 6-9 sweep parameters, but no model trained in one setting and tested in another is described.
q3_support: p. 14: "The conventional DNN has the highest RMSE, while the proposed CNN achieves the lowest RMSE." (learned DNN of [7], legend of Fig. 5(c), p. 13); p. 15: "AUG-DL scheme provides a curve that fits the average SE to" the non-learned AUG; RUG, NUG and brute force also compared.
q4_support: p. 16: "the DL (AUG-DL) approach can guarantee an execution time of under one second" (Table V: 0.34, 0.62, 0.89 s versus 74, 402, 1,150 s for AUG at 12, 24, 36 users); p. 13: "complexity of the proposed algorithm in Table II".
q5_support: p. 12: "whole dataset having 10K samples" is generated by solving problem (19) with Algorithm 2 on the authors' own simulator; no code or data link and no public dataset is given.
notes: STAR-RIS MIMO-NOMA SWIPT with short packets; the CNN imitates the iterative inner-approximation solution (learning to optimise). Included as area 3: it outputs precoder and phase shifts jointly with user grouping (grouping is above the physical layer but learned jointly with physical-layer decisions). q3 rests on the RMSE comparison with the DNN in [7] (Fig. 5(c) legend, read on the page image; [7] is the authors' earlier DL design) and on the SE comparison with the non-learned AUG, brute force, RUG and NUG; the SE of AUG-DL is not compared with a learned baseline. Tables II and V read on page images. Reviewer to confirm q3.
